applies_why: The text decides a collision between the challenger's seed/loins chain and the defender's chain, so K-C's chain-vs-chain rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — reading A: the judge may still note explicit naming as part of overall support; reading B: requiring a chain to name Joseph as begetter is an impermissible verse-by-verse/stating-verse test.
why: The judge treats the challenger's chain not naming Joseph as the begetter as a defect, which is the retired stating-verse/verse-by-verse test rather than a pure chain-footing comparison.
